title: Three Stickers and a Zombie Lesson
source_body:
Today, I taught English to a six-year-old boy.
He worked hard during the lesson and followed the activities well, so I gave him a sticker as a reward. We have a simple rule: if he collects three stickers, he can choose something fun to do during the next lesson.
Today, he finally collected his third sticker.
I expected him to choose a game or a small prize. Instead, he happily said that he wanted to play a zombie game.
For a moment, I wondered if I had made a terrible mistake.
Then things became even more interesting. His mother, who had been sitting quietly beside us, agreed to join the game. She said that she would become a zombie too.
So next week, I am supposed to teach English while being chased by a six-year-old zombie and his mother.
I am not sure how much English we will study that day.
Still, I have to admit that I am strangely looking forward to it.

variants.prestudy:
Today, I found myself teaching English to a six-year-old boy, one of the most energetic students I have ever taught.
Because he had worked hard throughout the lesson and had followed every activity with surprising focus, I rewarded him with a sticker. We follow a simple rule in class: once he collects three stickers, he is allowed to choose something enjoyable for the following lesson.
Today, much to his delight, he finally earned his third sticker.
Naturally, I assumed he would ask for a video game or perhaps a small toy. Instead, grinning from ear to ear, he announced that what he truly wanted was to play a zombie game.
For a brief, unsettling moment, it occurred to me that I might have made a rather serious mistake in agreeing to such a rule.
What happened next made the situation even more entertaining. His mother, who had been sitting quietly beside us the entire time, unexpectedly volunteered to join in. Smiling, she declared that she, too, would transform into a zombie for the occasion.
As a result, next week I am expected to teach an English lesson while being chased around the room by a six-year-old zombie and his equally enthusiastic mother.
Whether much English will actually be learned that day remains uncertain.
Even so, I must confess that, strangely enough, I find myself looking forward to it more than I probably should.
